MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, NOVEMBER 3, 2025

* The Planning Commission held a closed session meeting at 6:30 p.m. prior to the regular
agenda.

1.  CALL TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called
to order by CHAIR OLSON at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

CHAIR OLSON led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Olson, Nicklas, Medawar, Repp-Loadsman, Romanelli,
  Schachter, Yoo

  City Staff Present: Katrina Kawagoe, Senior Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst
  Steve McEwen, Assistant City Attorney

* Steve McEwen, Assistant City Attorney, stated that there is no reportable action from the
closed session meeting.

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, OCTOBER 6,
  2025

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER REPP-
LOADSMAN to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF OCTOBER 6,
  2025.

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL
  SUCH ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

COMMISSIONER  MEDAWAR  made  a  motion,  seconded  by  COMMISSIONER
SCHACHTER to,

  APPROVE ITEM 6A

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240540; ADDRESS: 19 Rollingwood Drive,
  Rolling Hills Estates, CA 90274; APPLICANT: Riad Itani, Seaside Designs; A request
  1
Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
November 3, 2025
   for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-240541) for rear yard
  improvements that include legalizing unpermitted retaining walls and a Grading
  Permit (G-240542) for the export of more than 20 cubic yards of earth materials and
  excavation greater than three feet in vertical height at its deepest point.

Katrina Kawagoe, Senior Planner, stated that Planning Application PA-240540 is a continued
item from the October 6 Planning Commission meeting, and proceeded to provide a
presentation summarizing the staff report. She provided an overview of the site and stated
that this is a code compliance case that was opened in 2024 for construction in the rear yard
without permits. The applicant is proposing to build a pool and spa at the foot of the slope
and in order to support this, a series of eight retaining walls and free-standing property line
walls were built. Following the October 6 meeting, the applicant decided to demolish the
walls along the east property line along the northwest corner that are encroaching within the
required two-foot setback; this action eliminates the requirement for a Variance. Senior
Planner Kawagoe presented the new rendering which will include added landscaping to
soften the walls, and the walls will be refinished in a lighter shade.

Senior Planner Kawagoe stated that staff have determined that the criteria for Neighborhood
Compatibility and approval of the Grading application have been met.

Senior Planner Kawagoe stated that staff recommend that the Planning Commission
approved Planning Application No. PA-240540 subject to the conditions outlined in the staff
report.

CHAIR OLSON read a statement regarding unapproved or unpermitted construction projects
that are presented to the Planning Commission for consideration.

VICE CHAIR NICKLAS asked for clarification on the building permit and plan check process
assuming this case moves forward. Senior Planner Kawagoe explained the process and
confirmed that the inspector will be involved in investigating that the wall is constructed
according to plan.

CHAIR OLSON inquired about the wall that was constructed in the easement and how far
the wall is in the easement. Senior Planner Kawagoe stated that the wall is approximately
four feet into the easement.

CHAIR OLSON asked if the fence or a guard rail behind the retaining wall would still be
required. Senior Planner Kawagoe stated that she believes it will still be required per the
building code.

CHAIR OLSON stated several concerns regarding meeting the criteria for Neighborhood
Compatibility and for approval of the Grading application.

Riat Itani, Applicant, addressed the question about the guard rail, by stating that the building
code related to this issue is subjective since this is typically required if there is a walking
surface between a building, deck, balcony, etc. Mr. Itani stated that he will go back to review
the building code to confirm if a guard rail is required for this project. In addition, he stated
that any grade difference of more than 30” requires a guard rail. He added that to meet the
requirement, a glass guard rail for visibility of the artistic features as shown in the rendering
and stated that this could be added as a condition of approval if required by the building
code.

VICE CHAIR NICKLAS asked if trees can be planted in front of the wall facing Silver Spur
Road. Mr. Itani stated that trees can be planted to camouflage the wall; however, he believes
that the project will be aesthetically pleasing. Mr. Itani stated that as part of the drainage
plan, they will be adding a sump pump to drain water up.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN asked about how much space there is to add
landscaping in front of the wall since this may be added as a condition of approval. Senior
Planner Kawagoe stated that it varies, but there is a minimum of approximately 5’ to 11’.

  2
Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
November 3, 2025
 COMMISSION YOO asked about the concern that staff have on building within the
easement. Assistant Attorney McEwen stated that staff examined this and is not concerned
with the proposed construction in the easement; the goal of the slope easement was to
ensure slope stability to protect Silver Spur Road below. This project would increase slope
stability. If an issue should arise, the City can still access the easement for the purpose of
slope stability to protect the right-of-way below. Mr. Itani confirmed that he is aware and
agrees with the slope easement.

CHAIR OLSON suggested that the conditions of approval as discussed be added as follows:
additional landscaping consisting of mature trees (at least 10’) be planted at the bottom of
the wall to soften the impact and mass and bulk of the walls; the addition of guard rails that
provide for 90% of light and air at the wall within the easement.

Mr. Itani stated that there are options outside of adding fencing around the pool that will
comply with the building code, and they will be opting for those options rather than adding
fencing around the pool.

CHAIR OLSON stated that the Planning Commission have expressed concern about the
slope stability and grading for the walls and their location; due to the walls being pre-built, he
would like to express concerns to the Building Official, regarding the construction of the walls
and the conditions of the soil. Assistant Attorney McEwen explained that this should not be
added as a condition of approval that the City is required to meet since this is a policy matter.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER commended the applicant for accommodating the requests
and working closely with the City. He stated that in the past, neighborhood compatibility in
regard to mass and scale is relative to the impact on neighbors; he stated that this project
does not impact neighboring property since the walls are only visible from Silver Spur Road.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR concurred.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
MEDAWAR to:

  APPROVE PA-250540, SUBJECT TO THE CONDITIONS OUTLINED IN THE
  STAFF REPORT AND THE CONDITIONS FOR ADDITIONAL LANDSCAPING AND
  INSTALLATION OF A GUARD RAIL.

Ayes: Nicklas, Medawar, Repp-Loadsman, Romanelli, Schachter
Noes: Olson, Yoo
Absent:
Abstain:

Administrative Analyst Corea stated that the Planning Commission has approved Planning
Application No. PA-240540, a request for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination for
rear yard improvements that include legalizing unpermitted retaining walls and a Grading
Permit for the export of more than 20 cubic yards of earth materials and excavation greater
than three feet in vertical height at its deepest point with the additional conditions for
additional landscaping and installation of a guard rail at 19 Rollingwood Drive in the City of
Rolling Hills Estates. There is a 20-day appeal period by which any member of the public or
the City Council, by its own motion, may appeal this project.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-250160; ADDRESS: 758 Silver Spur Road (Barte
  Earle Way), Rolling Hills Estates, CA 90274; APPLICANT: Mostafa Rahimi;
  DESCRIPTION: A request to amend a Conditional Use Permit No. 240140 (CUP-
  250159) for medical office use, to include oxygen therapy services, and a Precise
  Plan of Design (PPD-250161) for exterior improvements including the installation of
  related medical equipment.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR stated that he does not know Dr. Rahimi; however, he owns
a business down the street from the subject property.
  3
Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
November 3, 2025
 Katrina Kawagoe, Senior Planner provided a presentation for Planning Application No. PA-
250160 summarizing the staff report. The site received a Conditional Use Permit for medical
office use and a precise plan of design for unpermitted exterior improvements, including to
the facade of the building and a Variance to maintain less than 20% of landscaped area on
December 2, 2024. The applicant is proposing to amend the conditional use permit to include
oxygen therapy services. While the business plan is not changing from what was approved,
the plans did not reflect the installation of the oxygen tank enclosure at the rear of the building
Staff required that the applicants have mechanical engineering plans reviewed and were
cleared by the Los Angeles County Fire Department. Senior Planner Kawagoe stated that
the proposed location of the oxygen tank is in the rear parking area which will use one stall,
which will slightly alter the parking and landscape location, which requires a Precise Plan of
Design.

Senior Planner Kawagoe stated that staff have determined that this project does comply with
the requirements for approval of a Conditional Use Permit.

Senior Planner Kawagoe stated that the applicant is proposing a 169 SF oxygen tank
enclosure in the rear of the property, which will include a 5’-6” CMU block wall along the west
side and a chain link fence along the north and east side of the enclosure. The existing site
has nine parking spaces, however only seven are required. The proposed project will remove
one parking space for the oxygen tank and an additional parking space was removed to
widen the stalls, in order to meet the required stall size of 9’-20’.

Senior Planner Kawagoe stated that staff have determined that this project meets the criteria
to approve a Precise Plan of Design.

Senior Planner Kawagoe stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission open
the public hearing, take public testimony, discuss the issues, close the public hearing, and
adopt Resolution No. PA-250160 approving the project.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN inquired if the handicapped parking space should be
van accessible and if so, the loading zone may need to be 8’ rather than 5’. Senior Planner
Kawagoe stated that she will confirm this with the Building Official.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR stated that this property has been a challenge with drivers
exiting the property due to impaired visibility and inquired about a red curb for half of a
parking space in front of the property. He also recommended that the applicant ask his
patients to park on the street since it is more easily accessible and keep the rear parking for
staff.

CHAIR OLSON inquired about the condition of approval to address the failing wall in the rear
of the property. Senior Planner Kawagoe stated that a report from a structural engineer was
submitted, and this will be required prior to opening their business.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR
to,
  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

Michael Papayans, Designer, stated that the wall behind this property is not failing, rather it
is the wall behind Red Onion that is failing. COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR suggested
installing a French drain behind the wall.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR inquired about the need for the size of the oxygen tank. Dr.
Rahimi stated that there are two types of tanks for hyperbaric oxygen therapy – one is bulk,
which is 9,000 gallons and there are smaller tanks, but they need to be refilled more
frequently. The larger tank is more cost effective. He has owned this tank since 2018.

In response to a question from COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR, Dr. Rahimi stated that he was
the only one in the South Bay that had this type of oxygen tank with the exception of a
hospital in Long Beach. This tank is connected by cell tower directly to the fire department.
  4
Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
November 3, 2025
 Later the tank will need to be telemonitored. Dr. Rahimi stated that he does not know any
issues with these tanks and stated that they follow all the protocols from the Fire Department.
Senior Planner Kawagoe stated that the applicant submitted their plans to the Fire
Department and they were cleared for this hearing and they will be required to submit to their
Petro Chemical unit.

Dr. Rahimi stated that he would like to request a blue curb in front of the property. Senior
Planner Kawagoe stated that this will need to be directed to the Traffic and Safety Committee
for consideration.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
MEDAWAR to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. PA-250160, APPROVING THE PROJECT SUBJECT TO THE
  CONDITIONS OUTLINED IN THE STAFF REPORT.

Ayes: Olson, Nicklas, Medawar, Repp-Loadsman, Romanelli, Schachter, Yoo
Noes:
Absent:
Abstain:

The Planning Commission has approved PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-250160, a
resolution amending Conditional Use Permit No. PA-240140 for medical office use, to include
oxygen therapy services, and a Precise Plan of Design for exterior improvements including
the installation of related medical equipment at 758 Silver Spur Road (also known as Bart
Earle Way) in the City of Rolling Hills Estates. There is a 20-day appeal period by which any
member of the public or the City Council, by its own motion, may appeal this project.

9.  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

CHAIR OLSON expressed his concern that the project at 19 Rollingwood went unnoticed for as long
as it did and asked if the inspector has a responsibility to report any unpermitted work to the city.
Senior Planner Kawagoe stated that this typically falls under the purview of the Code Compliance
Officer, and the City operates on a reactionary basis. CHAIR OLSON stated that an inspector will
know if he has inspected the property. COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN stated that when work
is going on in the City, the inspector has a responsibility to at least check if there are permits for the
work. Senior Planner Kawagoe stated that when an inspector notices unpermitted work he/she will
issue a stop work notice. CHAIR OLSON expressed his concern that there have been four different
inspectors within the last eight months, which is concerning for continuity. CHAIR OLSON stated that
he has been made aware of issues with Willdan and inspectors.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that this should be brought up to the City Council when the
Willdan contract is up for review. COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN concurred and stated that
cities go through an RFP process prior to awarding a contract. This information should be submitted
to the director.

CHAIR OLSON asked if the City has done an end of building evaluation from homeowners. Senior
Planner Kawagoe stated that this is not generally a Planning Commission decision, however, she will
bring this to the attention of the Director.

COMMISSIONER YOO asked about rules for approving unpermitted work. COMMISSIONER REPP-
LOADSMAN recommended that this item be added to a future agenda for discussion.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR stated that the staging area for the Deep Valley Drive project has
impacted their street Silver Spur Road (Bart Earle Way). Senior Planner Kawagoe stated that she
will bring this to the Public Works Manager.

  5
Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
November 3, 2025
 10.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

NONE

11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, OCTOBER 14, 2025

  The PLANNING COMMSSION received and filed Item No. 11A.

Respectfully submitted by,  Approved,

Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst  Larry Olson, Chair
